subject: Capacity OKRs — launch traffic cadence & quota ask (BrightHealth PoC)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Asha Ramanathan <asha@brighthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity OKRs — launch traffic cadence & quota ask (BrightHealth PoC)

Team — quick heads-up and ask. BrightHealth (BH-7842) has confirmed a pilot window starting next Tuesday that will exercise our hosted API as close to production. They shared a short traffic profile (attached) and asked whether we can: (1) temporarily increase their ingress quota and soft rate limit for the pilot window, and (2) provide a recommended canary cadence so their SREs can ramp safely.

Summary of numbers from the customer forecast (attached):
- baseline: ~120 req/s (mostly short text-generation calls)
- expected sustained during business hours: 220 req/s
- peak bursts: 350–420 req/s for 2–5m windows (spikey but repeatable)
- ~30% of requests will use streaming + function-calls; KV cache usage unknown

Ask: can Product/Infra authorise a temporary quota uplift to 500 req/s for the pilot (region: us-west) with a required canary plan (start at 100–150 req/s for 30m, then 250 for 1h, then full traffic)? We need confirmation within 48 hours to lock routing and pre-warm caches.

Attachments: brighthealth_capacity_forecast_q3_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with hourly estimates).

Next steps I propose:
- Product: confirm acceptable max soft-limit and any recommended model variant or quantization profile.
- Infra: confirm routing changes, pre-warm timeline, and whether we can pin them to dedicated pool for the pilot.
- CS/Sales: confirm the pilot start date and whether we should offer temporary credit for burst usage.

Asha — tagging you so your eng lead can see the recommended canary cadence and tell us if the spike profile looks accurate.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Asha Ramanathan <asha@brighthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity OKRs — launch traffic cadence & quota ask (BrightHealth PoC)

Thanks Diego — acknowledging. A few clarifying Qs from CS before Product/Infra commits:
- Do we know which model variant they'll run? (large vs. medium quantized)
- Can they confirm whether the 30% streaming calls contain long-running streams (more than 30s)?
- Does BrightHealth want traffic split across regions or pinned to us-west? They indicated strict latency needs.

From a CS perspective I want a clear rollback trigger (error rate > 5% for 10m or p95 latency > 700ms) and a short canary that ramps conservatively. If Product can give us a canary checklist (metrics to watch + runbook), I'll own post-launch comms to the customer.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Capacity OKRs — launch traffic cadence & quota ask (BrightHealth PoC)

Adding commercial context — BrightHealth is currently in our enterprise pipeline (deal BH-7842). Their PO/contract is in progress; legal has a few redlines but finance expects sign-off this week. If Product/Infra are comfortable with a temporary uplift, Sales recommends we offer a one-week burst credit (up to $5k) as part of the pilot to reduce friction.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/3847290/BH-7842 — forecasted ARR if pilot converts is material enough that a short-term credit is fine.

If Infra needs a hard commit on traffic profile, I can ask BrightHealth to certify the spike windows (engineers can provide a sample script) — would that help pre-warm?

Thanks — Karthik
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Ramanathan <asha@brighthealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity OKRs — launch traffic cadence & quota ask (BrightHealth PoC)

On Wed, Sep 14, 2027 at 09:12 Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — quick heads-up and ask. BrightHealth (BH-7842) has confirmed a pilot window starting next Tuesday that will exercise our hosted API as close to production. They shared a short traffic profile (attached) and asked whether we can: (1) temporarily increase their ingress quota and soft rate limit for the pilot window, and (2) provide a recommended canary cadence so their SREs can ramp safely.

Thanks for the detail — Product has reviewed the forecast and we can support a temporary soft limit increase with the following constraints and checklist:

Temporary uplift
- Max soft limit for pilot (us-west): 500 req/s (soft throttle threshold; hard limit remains 600 req/s for safety)
- Canary cadence required: 1) 150 req/s for 30m, 2) 250 req/s for 1h, 3) increase to customer-requested levels with 15m observation windows between steps

Technical notes
- Preferred model: rwd-medium-q4 (quantized), unless customer needs the larger model for quality tests. If they want rwd-large, we need +24h to pre-warm and test KV cache behavior.
- Streaming: if streams exceed 30s, we throttle streams independently; please flag long streams early.
- KV caching: request a sample trace from BrightHealth so we can estimate cache hit-rate; high miss-rates will require more warm-up and could impact allowed burst size.

Operational runbook
- Infra to provision a temporary routing rule and pre-warm caches 12h before pilot window.
- CS to watch rollout metrics: p50/p95 latency, error rate, 5xx count, model GPU utilization.
- Rollback triggers: error rate >5% over 10m, p95 latency >700ms over 10m, or sustained GPU utilization >90% for 15m.

I'll attach the canary runbook (launch_canary_runbook_v2.pdf) and create a short infra ticket for the routing change. If Sales wants to offer a burst credit, Product is fine as long as finance signs off.

Action items
- Karthik: confirm whether we offer the one-week credit and log it in HubSpot.
- Monica: confirm rollback comms and who will be on call during the pilot.
- Diego: ask BrightHealth eng for sample request traces and confirm model variant.

Laura Bennett
Head of Product — Serving, Redwood Inference
